title: Client-driven heartbeat + windowed fragment ACK protocol for streaming responses
creator: Asha Menon
description: Problem: Current SSE implementation relies on server-driven chunk pacing and full-session resume tokens. In high-latency mobile networks or intermediary proxies, we see clients buffering indefinitely or issuing repeated full-session reconnects that increase tail latency and duplicate work. Goal: Introduce a client-driven lightweight flow-control + heartbeat and a windowed fragment ACK mechanism that minimizes re-transmit scope, preserves function-call and structured-output boundaries, and remains compatible with existing legacy SSE clients.
acceptance_criteria: Client and server exchange a small initial flow window (in bytes and logical fragments) on connect and on reconnect
Clients send periodic heartbeat frames (SSE comment lines) and explicit fragment-ACK frames to advance server window without requiring full session state transfer
Server re-sends only missing fragments since last acknowledged fragment id; function-call and JSON-structure boundaries are never split in retransmits
Legacy clients (no ACK support) continue to receive a compatible SSE event stream with no schema change; server can operate in mixed-mode
End-to-end tests demonstrate 60% reduction in re-sent tokens on flaky networks and no regressed 99th percentile latency under normal conditions
Implementation is feature-flagged and can be toggled in deployment; rollout plan includes canary and observability dashboards
technical_notes: Design uses logical fragment ids: 64-bit monotonically increasing IDs per stream. IDs are encoded in chunk metadata as 'X-Redwood-Fragment-Id' in initial event comment or as a small envelope preceding JSON payload
Flow window expressed as 'available_fragments' and 'available_bytes' on connect; server enforces window for optimistic backpressure

Client heartbeat is an SSE comment line starting with ':hb <timestamp> <client-cid>' sent at configurable interval (default 15s). Heartbeat also carries last_ack_id in a small encoded token when possible
ACK frame is an idempotent SSE event type 'ack' with data: last_ack_id and optional checksum. Server treats ack as advancing durable ack watermark for that stream/customer

On reconnect the client supplies last_ack_id; server calculates minimal range to re-send and emits a 'recovery' envelope that contains fragment-ids for resend candidates. Fragment reassembly ensures function-call frames are whole: server must re-emit earlier fragment that contains the function-call start if any unacked fragments overlap that boundary

Compatibility: For clients that do not send ACKs, server falls back to legacy streaming behavior and emits periodic 'continuity' checkpoints every N fragments to make eventual reconnection less stateful
Metrics to add: ack_rate, avg_retx_fragments_per_reconnect, hb_liveness_missed_count, fragment_window_utilization, functioncall_boundary_retx_count
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Spike, 1 week): Prototype wire format in dev environment; implement client-side minimal ACK+heartbeat; build server sim harness to assert retransmit minimization

Phase 2 (Core impl, 3 weeks): Implement fragment-id tagging in runtime encoder, server-side window enforcement and ack processing, preservation of function-call/JSON structural boundaries during retransmit
Phase 3 (Compat & Rollout, 2 weeks): Add mixed-mode compat layer for legacy clients, feature flag gating, and migration docs for SDKs
Phase 4 (Canary + Observability, 1 week): Deploy to canary cohort, add dashboards, set automated rollback triggers if retx increases or hb misses spike
Phase 5 (SDK updates & Docs, 1 week): Publish SDK client changes for JS/Python/Go, update API docs and example apps
dependencies: ENG-614302 - runtime encoder hooks for fragment metadata
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Fragment-id space growth and storage of unacked windows may increase memory pressure on long-lived streams. Mitigation: cap window size per-stream and evict oldest unacked fragments with explicit 'abandon' diagnostic event when exchange falls behind

Risk: Proxies or intermediaries strip SSE comments or event types. Mitigation: fall back to legacy behavior and detect stripping by monitoring hb_liveness_missed_count; document required proxy settings for enterprise deployments

Risk: Small risk of breaking function-call atomicity on mishandled retransmits. Mitigation: server enforces 'boundary-first' retransmit rules and unit tests validate function-call grammar preservation
test_plan: Unit tests: fragment id generation, ack id advancement, boundary-aware retransmit selection
Integration tests: simulated flaky network with packet loss and delayed reconnects; assert re-sent token counts and structured output integrity
Load tests: validate 99th percentile latency for streaming under normal traffic with windowing enabled
Backward compatibility tests: verify legacy clients receive identical output ordering and that mixed-mode streams do not deadlock
Chaos test: introduce proxy that strips comments to ensure server detects and falls back cleanly
monitoring_and_alerting: New dashboards: stream_ack_lag (per model), avg_retransmit_fragments, heartbeat_missed_rate
Alerts: heartbeat_missed_rate > 2% for 5m in a customer cohort => Pager
SLO checks: streaming delivery success rate (not counting deliberate partial outputs) >= 99.9%
Rollback triggers: avg_retx_fragments_per_reconnect increases > 3x baseline during canary
migration_notes: SDKs: add optional 'enableWindowedAck' flag defaulting to false for the initial rollout; server will advertise capability in initial connect comment
Docs: publish migration guide showing minimal client changes (send ':hb' comments and 'ack' events) and how to interpret server recovery envelopes
Enterprise: note proxy configuration and load-balancer idle timeouts that may affect SSE comment preservation
